segments.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for having me today.
I'm here to talk about how we can transform our customer experience through simplicity.
Last year, our team spent over 4,000 hours responding to customer support tickets.
That's because our product had become too complex. Too many features, too many clicks, too many options.
So we asked ourselves: What if we focused on doing one thing really well?
First, we identified the core use case. The one thing 80% of our customers needed.
Second, we stripped away everything that didn't serve that core need.
And finally, we tested the new design with real customers every single week.
Let me tell you a quick story. One of our enterprise customers, Sarah, had been struggling for months.
She told us: I used to spend 20 minutes setting up each campaign. Now it takes 2 minutes.
That's the power of simplicity. When you remove friction, you create value.
The results speak for themselves. Support tickets dropped by 60%.
Customer satisfaction scores jumped from 3.2 to 4.7 out of 5.
And our net promoter score went from 12 to 52 in just six months.
Now, you might be thinking: But what about power users? Won't they miss those advanced features?
Great question. We found that 95% of power users were only using 3 advanced features.
So we kept those three and tucked them under an Advanced menu. Problem solved.
So to summarize: Focus on the core need. Remove everything else. Test relentlessly.
Simplicity isn't about doing less. It's about doing what matters.
I challenge each of you: Go back to your teams and ask, what can we remove?
Start with one feature, one workflow, one screen. Simplify it. Measure the impact.
If you do that, I promise you'll see the same results we did.
Thank you. I'm happy to take any questions.
Yes, let me repeat the question. How do we decide which features to cut?
